summary: Express's own final handler still writes body-parser/status errors (e.g. malformed JSON, 400) to stderr via console.error as unstructured text, outside the logger and without requestId. Node's JSON.parse message can echo a snippet of the request body ("Unexpected token ..., \"{not json B\"... is not valid JSON"), so a body fragment can reach stderr. server.ts only owns the no-status branch; status errors are passed to next(err) unchanged by design (client response must not change).
evidence: apps/api/src/composition/request-log.test.ts redaction test: POST /ask with body '{not json ...' prints a SyntaxError stack to stderr from body-parser during the test run.
fix_direction: Add an explicit handler for status-carrying errors that logs structured (message scrubbed/omitted) with requestId and then responds with the same status/body as Express's default; needs a decision on the client body (default page leaks stack outside production).

summary: Other apps/api code (routes, indexing, ingest-store, whatsapp/store) still uses console.*; those lines bypass redaction and requestId. Left for the route lanes; routes can use req.log.
fix_direction: Replace with req.log / logger from composition/logger.ts.

summary: The test-mode default (silent under node --test when LOG_LEVEL unset) has no test for either branch, so the worst regression survives: dropping the NODE_TEST_CONTEXT condition (if (!v) return silent) makes a production process with LOG_LEVEL unset log NOTHING, and all 8 request-log tests still pass. The only resolveLevel assertions are explicit values and nonsense->info.
evidence: Checker mutation M6 on apps/api/src/composition/logger.ts resolveLevel: '!v && process.env.NODE_TEST_CONTEXT' -> '!v'; request-log.test.ts exit 0 (SURVIVED). The always-true variant (M5) is killed only incidentally via the nonsense assertion.
fix_direction: Add a test that saves/restores process.env: with LOG_LEVEL unset and NODE_TEST_CONTEXT deleted, resolveLevel(undefined) is info; with NODE_TEST_CONTEXT set and LOG_LEVEL unset it is silent; with LOG_LEVEL=info it is info even under test context.

summary: Redaction is a key deny-list plus string patterns, not an allow-list. Probed leaks (no current caller logs these shapes): fields named rawKey/accessKey/bearer/auth/jwt are not redacted by key; a bare string value like /search?q=SECRET (no scheme, no leading whitespace) keeps its query; Authorization: Basic X leaks X; URL-encoded Bearer%20X leaks; mongodb://u:p@w@h and mongodb://u:p/w@h (invalid, unescaped) leave part of the password; a Buffer field is emitted as byte numbers; a bare secret in free text is unscrubbable by construction.
evidence: checker probe, 33 cases; 9 leak the fake secret, none via the access line or error handler as wired today
fix_direction: Hardening: add key patterns (raw|access)?key, bearer, auth, jwt, session; scrub bare path?query strings; keep logged fields allow-listed at call sites.
